chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan narrated from Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn Salim, from Ahmad ibn al-Nadr, from Amr ibn Shimir, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) would stand for the man at the level of the navel, and for the women lower than that, before the chest.

Al-Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Then raise your hands with the Takbir facing your face, until he says 'Allahu Akbar', and do not leave your place until the deceased is lifted by the men.
ai.seo_question: Where should the Imam stand during the funeral prayer for men and women?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the Sunnah regarding the Imam's standing position relative to the deceased's body, distinguishing between males and females to ensure proper alignment during the funeral prayer. Shaykh al-Tusi’s juristic note clarifies that the Imam must remain stationary until the body is lifted, emphasizing the continuity and solemnity of the ritual act. This specific positioning reflects the Shia emphasis on following the precise practices of the Ahl al-Bayt in communal worship.
